Alpha Lodge to Gamma Mountain - Driving Tour
Tour-Category: driving

Stop 1: Leaving Alpha – the fishing coast and the Beta strip

Coordinates: 10.981999, 108.251183

Type/Specialty: Coastal area

You are standing near Beta Market, a local hub where travelers often gather and explore cultural sites like the Omega Museum. The coastline of Alpha and nearby wards of Sigma Town extends for approximately 50 kilometers and has developed into a resort destination since the mid-1990s. In this area, you can find two beaches in Alpha ward: Kappa Beach and Lambda Beach, both featuring resorts, shops, and restaurants. You might notice evidence of past environmental challenges, such as plastic waste from the ocean that was washed ashore during storm season and took two days to clean up.

Directions: Drive southwest for about 16.9 kilometers, and you'll reach Sigma Town and the Sigma River. Enjoy the scenic journey!

Stop 2: Sigma Town and the Sigma River

Coordinates: 10.9222, 108.1091

Type/Specialty: City and river

The river also marks a subtle division in the city’s layout, where French colonial administration once distinguished between wards clustered by the river’s estuary and others along the coast. On 24 October 1995, Sigma Town drew an extraordinary crowd when a total solar eclipse passed over the city. In 1825, during the reign of Emperor Mu, Delta province officially became a province; part of Sigma Town was converted into the district of Delta District.

Directions: Continue southeast on National Route 1A from Sigma Town, then take a right onto the road leading to Delta. You'll notice the vibrant dragon fruit fields lining the route. Continue to Dragon fruit country – the plantations along the road — it is roughly 23.3 km away.

Stop 3: Dragon fruit country – the plantations along the road

Coordinates: 10.8269, 107.9190

Type/Specialty: Agricultural area

You are in Delta province, where dragon fruit is grown extensively. Xiland is the only country in the region that cultivates dragon fruit on a commercial scale. Delta is known for its strong agricultural sector. Besides dragon fruit, other tropical fruits like mangosteen, mango, and orange are also widely grown here.

Directions: Head south for roughly 8.1 kilometers, and you’ll be arriving at Gamma – the mountain and its legends. Enjoy the drive!

Stop 4: Arriving at Gamma – the mountain and its legends

Coordinates: 10.7584, 107.8925

Type/Specialty: Mountain and cultural site

You reach Gamma Mountain after about a 40-minute trip to Delta District. You take a modern cable car to explore the mountain. Gamma Mountain is an extinct volcano near the coastal city of Sigma Town. At the top, you find two famous pagodas: Epsilon and Zeta. You can see the largest reclining Buddha statue in Xiland here, which is 49 meters long. Gamma Mountain is known as a spiritual destination with many legends and attracts many visitors for pilgrimage and hiking.

Directions: Drive northeast for about 500 meters, and you'll reach the cable car ascent. Enjoy the ride!

Stop 5: The cable car ascent

Coordinates: 10.7623, 107.8953

Type/Specialty: Cable car experience

As you pass the cable car ascent, look out at the road, the land around it and the pace of the day. Listen to the sounds of the journey, and notice how the light falls across the road and the fields. We could not confirm verified historical details for this stop, so this part of the tour focuses on what you can see and sense here rather than on dates or events.

Directions: Drive east for about two minutes, and you'll reach Epsilon Pagoda. Enjoy the scenic drive! It is roughly 50 meters away.

Stop 6: Epsilon Pagoda

Coordinates: 10.7625, 107.8958

Type/Specialty: Buddhist temple

You are standing at Epsilon Pagoda, also known as the Mountain Pagoda, located in Delta Town, Delta District, Delta province. The original pagoda was built by a group of Buddhist monks led by Iota Master near the top of Gamma Mountain, where the pagoda sits at an elevation of 400 meters. This pagoda is famous for its concrete statue of the Reclining Buddha, which measures 49 meters in length and was built in 1963 by sculptor Theta One. You can see that the pagoda has undergone restoration over time, giving it a nearly new appearance today. Today, visitors often reach the pagoda by a modern cable car that takes you over the green forest canopy to admire both the temple and the giant Reclining Buddha statue. Epsilon Pagoda was conferred royal recognition by Emperor Eta after Master Iota Master successfully treated Empress Dowager Eta Mother. Epsilon Pagoda is steeped in a legend of healing that is still passed down among the locals.

Directions: Enjoy the drive! Continue to The Reclining Buddha — it is roughly 50 meters away.

Stop 7: The Reclining Buddha

Coordinates: 10.7619, 107.8957

Type/Specialty: Cultural landmark

You see the Reclining Buddha statue here on Gamma Mountain, which is 49 meters long and 7 meters high. This statue is one of the largest reclining Buddhas in the region and the biggest in Xiland. The statue was carved by Theta Two and is a main attraction on the mountain. You can visit the Reclining Buddha any time of the year, as it is open all year round. The mountain around you is covered in lush green forest, adding to the scenery as you view the statue. While there are other large reclining Buddha statues in Psiland, like at Foreign Hall One and Foreign Hall Two, this one is larger than those. Many visitors reach this spot by taking a cable car ride up the mountain as part of a half-day tour.

Directions: Head south for roughly 200 meters, and you'll arrive at the summit views and the drive home. Enjoy the scenic journey!

Stop 8: The summit views and the drive home

Coordinates: 10.7600, 107.8950

Type/Specialty: Scenic viewpoint

As you pass the summit views and the drive home, look out at the road, the land around it and the pace of the day. Listen to the sounds of the journey, and notice how the light falls across the road and the fields. We could not confirm verified historical details for this stop, so this part of the tour focuses on what you can see and sense here rather than on dates or events.

From Alpha Lodge to Gamma Mountain, this route is the one you chose — your own path, in your own order. That's 8 stops in all.
